qa_pairs.question: What are the steps to install the necessary Ceph client packages and their repositories on a Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) family system?
qa_pairs.answer: To install the Ceph client packages on a RHEL-based system, first install the Extra Packages for Enterprise Linux (EPEL) repository using `sudo dnf install epel-release`. If you are running el10, temporarily disable the default cryptographic policy with `sudo update-crypto-policies --set LEGACY`. Next, import the Ceph project's public key using `sudo rpm --import 'https://download.ceph.com/keys/release.asc'`. Finally, install the Ceph client and its dependencies with `sudo dnf install -y libcephfs2 python3-cephfs ceph-common python3-ceph-argparse`. If the cryptographic policy was temporarily disabled, remember to restore it afterwards with `sudo update-crypto-policies --set DEFAULT`.

qa_pairs.question: How can one install the Ceph client and its dependencies on a Debian-based Linux system?
qa_pairs.answer: For Debian-based systems, first add the Ceph repository by using `sudo apt-add-repository 'deb https://download.ceph.com/debian-tentacle/ {codename} main'`, replacing `{codename}` with your distro's codename (which can be found using `lsb_release -sc`). If this command results in an error, revert it with `sudo add-apt-repository -r 'deb https://download.ceph.com/debian-tentacle/ {codename} main'` and proceed to the next step. After adding the repository, install the ceph lib, cephfs client, and other dependencies using `sudo apt-get install -y libcephfs2 python3-cephfs ceph-common python3-ceph-argparse`.

qa_pairs.question: How do you configure the `ceph.conf` file for a Ceph client on the Arbutus cloud environment?
qa_pairs.answer:
To configure the Ceph client on Arbutus, you need to create the `/etc/ceph/ceph.conf` file with the following content:
```ini
[global]
admin socket = /var/run/ceph/$cluster-$name-$pid.asok
client reconnect stale = true
debug client = 0/2
fuse big writes = true
mon host = [v2:134.87.15.61:3300/0,v1:134.87.15.61:6789/0] [v2:134.87.15.62:3300/0,v1:134.87.15.62:6789/0] [v2:134.87.15.63:3300/0,v1:134.87.15.63:6789/0]
[client]
quota = true
```
This file specifies global settings and the monitor hosts for the Arbutus cloud.
